- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often overcorrects downward — raise forecast gently to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) — cap forecast rise to 5-7% above peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- In 30-day horizon, model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent 7-day avg is > 10% above 30-day moving avg.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.10 → -0.10 → +0.10), model tends to lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to capture momentum shift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 2–3% above model, apply 1.5–2.5% upward bias for next forecast if sentiment remains neutral or mildly bullish.
